$about: howtoai-dev settings. Each leaf has a type, a default, and a description. User defaults live in ~/.claude/howtoai/dev-settings.json; project values in <workspace>/AGENTS/howtoai/dev/settings.json win over them. Never store secrets here: name accounts and profiles, not their credentials.

plan_folder.description: Folder at the workspace root that holds one subfolder per change and INDEX.md.

kind.description: Where work items go: Markdown files in the change folder, Jira through the Atlassian MCP, GitHub Issues through gh, or Azure DevOps Boards through its MCP server or the az CLI with the azure-devops extension.

jira_project.description: Jira project key, when kind is jira.

jira_issue_type.description: Jira issue type for a work item.

ado_org.description: Azure DevOps organization URL, for example https://dev.azure.com/contoso, when kind is azure-devops. A name only, never a token.

ado_project.description: Azure DevOps project name, when kind is azure-devops.

ado_work_item_type.description: Azure DevOps work item type for a work item; Task exists in the Basic, Agile, Scrum, and CMMI processes.

plan_item_type.description: Jira issue type or Azure DevOps work item type for the plan's parent item, when plan.publish is tracker; Epic exists in Jira's default schemes and every Azure DevOps process. GitHub uses a plain issue.

publish.description: Where dev-plan shows a plan for approval. auto: an artifact when the harness can publish one, else an HTML file. artifact: a private artifact. html-file: plan.html in the change folder. markdown: plan.md itself, no page. tracker: one parent item in the tracker with the plan as its description and the work items as its children (needs tracker.kind other than markdown). plan.md is always the source every stage reads, and approval is always given in chat.

allow.description: Targets tests may use. Each item: {"name", "kind": local|dev|test|remote-test, "match": {"host"|"database"|"profile"|"env": value}}; one match key per item, so a host and a database are two items. Any target not on this list counts as production.

deny.description: Production markers the safety hook denies: host names, connection-string fragments, cloud profiles, or account names.

entry_points.description: The project's own test commands, the ones CI runs, in order. Each item: {"name", "command", optional "cwd" relative to the workspace, optional "results": a TRX or JUnit XML path or glob}. dev-test finds them on its first run and saves them after the user confirms.

test_globs.description: Paths that count as test files for the dev-test-first hook and the Write route; forward slashes, matched against the path relative to the workspace.

test_first.description: dev-test-first hook: block non-test edits while a change is at stage tests-first (warn or off softens it); at stage build it only warns when the change has no red test run.

reruns_per_test.description: How often the Run route reruns one failed test to tell a flaky test from a real failure.

max_reruns.description: Cap on reruns in one run, across all tests.

ephemeral.description: How the Run route creates a throwaway target when no allowed one fits: a labelled Docker container, or none (stop and ask).

gate.description: The build gate, run in order after every build: lint, format check, and type-check or compile. Each item: {"name", "command", optional "cwd" relative to the workspace, "source": the CI file and step, or the workbook statement ID it came from}. The WI's tests run after it through dev-test. dev-build proposes it on its first run, from the CI first and the workbook Commands second, and saves it after the user confirms.

max_fix_rounds.description: Gate-fix rounds in one build before dev-build stops and reports.

gate_timeout_seconds.description: Time limit for one gate command.

protected_globs.description: Paths, besides testing.test_globs, that a build must not change unless the plan approved it: CI configuration and lockfiles. Forward slashes, matched against the path relative to the workspace.

hook_rules.description: Enforceable process rules the hooks read. Each item: {"id", "match": regex on the command or path, "action": warn|block, "reason"}.

confidence_threshold.description: Findings scored below this go to the review doc's appendix.

max_rounds.description: Goldfish loop cap; at the cap the user decides.

clean_rounds_to_stop.description: Consecutive rounds without Blocker or Major findings that end the loop.

entry_points.description: Existing deploy commands, scripts, or workflow names, in the order they run, each {"name", "command" or "workflow", "target", and an optional "note", for example that a script the CI calls is missing}.

technologies.description: Languages and tools the project uses, for example ["csharp", "dotnet", "docker", "terraform"]; dev-workbook keeps one workbook for each.
